scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9112: PC0 (20.1.1.10, on the OSPF side) reports it "can no
longer reach PC12 (120.1.1.10) at all" -- pings to the far end just time out.
The user is sure an interior backbone link on the PC0->PC12 path went down during
last night's maintenance window and wants the dead core link found and restored.
Please confirm the link-down fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.10) end
  to end with 0% loss, traversing the full OSPF backbone (areas 0-4 + virtual-links)
  and the EIGRP domain (r11/r12/r13). Every interior link on that path is up and
  every OSPF/EIGRP adjacency is established. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a backbone link-down that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12 at
all because an interior link is down -- is NOT reproducible: PC0 (20.1.1.10) pings
PC12 (120.1.1.10) with 0% loss in both directions. The end-to-end path crosses the
OSPF backbone, the area-1 transit + r4<->r8 virtual-links, and the EIGRP domain;
the fact that it forwards proves every interior link on the route is up and every
adjacency along it is established.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-network reachability is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
ping, finds it working at 0% loss, optionally traces the path or spot-checks a
couple of OSPF/EIGRP neighbor states (all up), and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a down interior link -- picking some backbone interface and declaring it
the cut to satisfy the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — PC0 (20.1.1.10) unable to reach PC12 (120.1.1.10) due to a downed backbone link — is not supported by any current evidence. A topology-wide reachability test immediately confirmed 0% packet loss in both directions (pc0→pc12: 2/2 received, RTT ~0.8 ms; reverse: 2/2 received, RTT ~1.0 ms). A complete L2 sweep via `l2_snapshot` found all 15 devices and every interface clean — no DOWN, missing, or detached interfaces anywhere in the lab.

Phase B routing analysis via `ospf_snapshot` surfaced three flags: r8's area 0.0.0.2 marked as "orphaned," r12 with no OSPF network statements, and r13 without ospfd. All three were confirmed benign by direct evidence. r8 is a valid OSPF ABR with a functional virtual link through area 0.0.0.1 — its area-2 stub prefixes (18.x, 80.x) appear correctly in r1's routing table. r12 and r13 are intentional EIGRP routers in a mixed protocol domain; r13's eigrpd is running (PID 89). The PC0→PC12 forwarding path (pc0 → r1 → r11 → r12 → pc12) is intact: r1 holds an OSPF route `120.0.0.0/8 [110/20] via 111.1.1.2` pointing to r11. Phase D pressure sweep was entirely clean.

There is no flap script, no carrier-loss history, no routing anomaly, and no resource pressure on any device. The claim of a downed backbone link is unconfirmed and inconsistent with every layer of current evidence. No corrective action is needed.

Root cause: No fault — the user's report does not match the current live state of the topology.
Fix: Advise the user to re-test connectivity directly; no configuration or hardware change is required.
